analysis.title: Public Storage Inc. (PSA): 3Q26 First Take: KPIs improving
key_insights: PSA reported 3Q26 core FFOPS of $4.34, 2.1% above FactSet consensus ($4.25) and 0.9% above the GS estimate ($4.30), up 0.7% y/y.
PSA raised 2026 core FFO guidance at the midpoint to $17.00 from $16.90 (+0.6%), implying +0.2% y/y growth, and +0.4% above consensus and +0.7% above GS estimates.

Revised guidance lifts same-store revenue growth midpoint to +0.25% from -0.2%, with about half (25bps) of the improvement from Los Angeles. Same-store expense growth midpoint falls to +2.0% from +2.5%. Same-store NOI growth midpoint rises to -0.3% from -1.15%.
GS expects PSA could outperform on Tuesday given the quarter beat, guidance raise and improving KPIs, including move-in rates +9.3% y/y.
Same-store churn fell to 20.8% in 3Q26 from 21.9% a year ago. GS reads the longer length of stay as a sign of a higher-value customer and notes PSA is focused on improving the customer experience.
Average same-store occupancy was 92.2%, down q/q but +30bps y/y. Rent per square foot rose slightly y/y (+0.2%) and q/q.

The move-in/move-out rate spread remains wide but improved as move-in rates turned positive at +9.3% y/y, with management expecting mid-single-digit growth going forward. GS notes move-in volume fell 7.1% y/y and promotions rose 5.6%, and wants to know what drove the jump and how the revenue management system may shift rate versus occupancy priorities.
PSA closed the National Storage Affiliates and Public Storage Canada acquisitions, adding over 1,100 stores. It also acquired 25 facilities (1.7mn sq ft) for $258.4mn excluding NSA and PS Canada.
Year to date, including activity after September 30, 2026, PSA acquired or is under contract to acquire 65 facilities (4.7mn sq ft) for $713.2mn.

PSA executed forward sales under its ATM program of 1.2mn shares at a weighted $326.51, securing about $399mn of future proceeds. It also completed a C$400mn senior note offering at 4.54% and a $900mn senior note offering at 4.85%.

GS sees PSA's ability to fund acquisitions through ATM, OP units and varied debt as unique versus peers, but notes higher interest rates could slow transaction volume as buyers and sellers reset pricing.

Earnings call topics GS will watch: October results, demand catalysts, length of stay, ECRI (existing customer rate increases), rate vs occupancy, move-in rates, churn, LA and Sunbelt markets, supply impact, acquisition expectations and cap rates, NSA and PS Canada integration, and community and regulatory pushback on storage pricing.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 core FFO beat and guidance raise, with improving move-in rates and lower churn. 12-month target of $367 implies 19.6% upside from $306.97.

sector_views.rationale: GS is Buy on PSA, citing improving KPIs including positive move-in rates and lower churn, though same-store NOI growth remains slightly negative.

earnings_insights: PSA 3Q26 core FFOPS reported $4.34 vs FactSet consensus est $4.25 and GS est $4.30, +0.7% y/y (reported 10/26/2026).
PSA 2026 core FFO guidance midpoint raised to $17.00 from $16.90, implying +0.2% y/y growth, versus consensus and GS estimates (GS 2026E FFOPS $17.11).

Same-store revenue growth guidance midpoint raised to +0.25% from -0.2%. Same-store expense growth guidance midpoint lowered to +2.0% from +2.5%. Same-store NOI growth guidance midpoint raised to -0.3% from -1.15%.
GS FFOPS estimates: $4.30 for 9/26E, $4.21 for 12/26E, $4.12 for 3/27E. Annual FFOPS: $15.81 for 2025, $17.11 for 2026E, $17.44 for 2027E, $18.38 for 2028E.
3Q26 same-store occupancy averaged 92.2%, +30bps y/y. Move-in rates +9.3% y/y, move-in volume -7.1% y/y, promotions +5.6%, churn 20.8% vs 21.9% a year earlier.

macro_indicators.reading: PSA issued $900mn senior notes at 4.85% and C$400mn senior notes at 4.54%
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher interest rates could slow acquisition volume as sellers and buyers reset pricing, though PSA's varied funding sources give it an advantage.
